messages.subject: vectorized probit
parts:
Hello all. I am pretty new to Stan and am having some trouble implementing some of my jags models. I'd like to estimate a probit with k input variables. In bugs something like:

model{
for (i in 1:n) {
    y[i] ~ dbern(p[i])
    probit(p[i]) <- xbeta[i]
    xbeta[i] <- inprod(B[], X[i, ])
}
for(k in 1:K) {B[k] ~ dnorm(0, .1)}
}

My Stan code (using the birthwt data in MCMCpack) is:

library(rstan)
library(MCMCpack)
data(birthwt)

x <- as.matrix(cbind(1, birthwt$smoke, birthwt$ptl, birthwt$age))
birthwt_data <- list('N' = nrow(x), 'y' = birthwt$low, 'x' = x, 'K' = ncol(x))

birthwt_code <- '
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N,K] x;
  vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
  vector[K] beta;
}
model {
  for(n in 1:N) {
    for(k in 1:K) {
      y[n] ~ bernoulli(Phi(x[n,k] * beta[k]));
    }
  }
}
'
fit <- stan(model_code = birthwt_code, data = birthwt_data, iter = 1000, chains = 4)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: vectorized probit
parts:
On Friday, December 14, 2012 1:18:47 PM UTC-5, Zachary Jones wrote:
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N,K] x;
  vector[N] y;

I think bernoulli() requires y to be of integer type, which is only possible if it is declared as

int y[N];

because we do not have integer vectors / matrices / etc. currently. But you shouldn't need to change the rest of your code.

Relatedly, can I not use vectorization like

y ~ bernoulli(Phi(x * beta));

which seems to work fine when y is normally distributed? I couldn't get that to work either.

Only continuous densities are vectorized in v1.0.3; some discrete densities will be vectorized in v1.0.4. But I don't think Phi() will be vectorized in v1.0.4. Probably the fastest route that works currently is

model {
  vector[N] mu;
  mu <- x * beta;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    mu[n] <- Phi(mu[n]);
    y[n] ~ bernoulli(mu[n]); // omit this line in Stan >= v1.0.4
  }
//  y ~ bernoulli(mu);       // uncomment this line in Stan >= v1.0.4
}

Ben
